hook: ChatGPT just gave me a 47-step plan when I asked for help with one email.
caption:
ChatGPT just gave me a 47-step plan when I asked for help with one email.

I asked for help writing a follow-up to a client who went quiet.

What I got: a breakdown of email psychology, four different tonal approaches, a note about cultural communication differences, and a suggestion to "consider your relationship history."

Bro. I just need the email.

Here's the thing — AI doesn't know if you're a "just give me the answer" person or an "explain everything" person. So it hedges. It covers all bases. It writes for everyone, which means it writes for no one.

The fix isn't a better prompt. It's a profile.

When your AI knows you're a direct executor (not a researcher, not a brainstormer — someone who decides fast and moves) it stops padding. It stops offering options you didn't ask for. It stops teaching you things you already know.

One of the 8 thinking styles we map at bootfile.ai is exactly this: the person who needs outputs, not explanations. Short. Decided. Done.

If you've ever deleted more of an AI response than you kept — this is why.

Your bootfile fixes it at the source.
